# Hex: the complete reference

One plain-Markdown file for AI assistants and search engines. Hex is a free,
open-source voice appliance from Anomaly: local dictation, no-bot meeting
transcription, screen capture, and a read-only MCP server for agents. Every
claim here matches what Hex ships today; beta status is stated where it
applies.

- Site: https://anoma.ly/hex/
- Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/hex (MIT)
- Author: Anomaly, https://anoma.ly
- Latest stable release notes: https://anoma.ly/hex/changelog
- Agent index: https://anoma.ly/hex/llms.txt
- Agent skill: https://anoma.ly/hex/skill.md

## The short answer

Hex turns speech into text on the machine it runs on. Hold one shortcut, speak,
release; Hex transcribes with a local speech model and pastes the text wherever
the cursor is. It is free, open source, and works with no account and no network
once a model is downloaded.

Hex also records meetings without a bot. It captures the microphone and the
system audio itself, so there is no participant to invite and nothing
joins the call. Transcripts, live chapters, and stored notes stay in a local
folder with a retention you choose. `hex mcp` exposes those recordings to
OpenCode, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and any other MCP client, read
only.

## Platforms and requirements

- macOS 15 or later on Apple silicon. The stable build; Apple Speech is
  available as a model.
- Windows 10 and 11, x64 and ARM64. Beta.
- Linux, x86_64 and aarch64. Beta. X11 and compatible Wayland desktops through
  portals; see the Linux guide for the exact input and clipboard paths.
- iOS 18 or later: Hex's keyboard, on the App Store.
- Android 12 or later: Hex Preview, outside Google Play.

The command line, read-only history and meetings queries, and `hex mcp` run on
macOS, Linux, and Windows. Meetings is in the sidebar on all three, off until
you turn it on; another machine can read a mirrored meetings folder with
`--meetings-dir`.

## Install

Mac:

```sh
brew install --cask anomalyco/tap/hex
# or download the DMG
# https://anoma.ly/hex/download/macos-arm64-dmg
```

Windows beta (x64; use windows-arm64-setup for ARM64):

```
https://anoma.ly/hex/download/windows-x64-setup
```

Linux beta:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://anoma.ly/hex/install-linux.sh | sh
```

Linux packages and binaries are on https://anoma.ly/hex, including .deb, .rpm,
Nix (`nix profile add github:anomalyco/hex`), and AUR (`yay -S hex-bin`).

On macOS the `hex` command lives inside the app. Homebrew links it; otherwise:

```sh
ln -s /Applications/Hex.app/Contents/MacOS/hex ~/.local/bin/hex
```

Linux and Windows installs put `hex` on the PATH.

## Dictation

- Hold the shortcut, speak, release. Hex shows a small capsule while it listens
  and pastes the transcript into the focused app when it is done.
- Pre-roll and a release tail keep the first and last words; the audio timeline
  is authoritative even when the UI or another process stalls.
- Modes and Output steps decide what is pasted: built-in cleanup, word
  replacements, an optional AI rewrite, and transforms.
- The last dictation can be pasted again with Paste Last (Option-Shift-V on the
  Mac).
- History keeps recent dictations for 7 days by default, up to 10,000 entries
  or 16 MiB. Dictation audio is not stored unless Keep recordings is turned on.

## Models

Hex runs speech recognition locally. The catalog includes Parakeet and Whisper
GGUF models for dictation on macOS, Windows, and Linux, and Apple Speech on the
Mac. Models download once and then run offline. A model can be chosen in
Settings, installed with the model commands, or added as a custom GGUF or from
Hugging Face. One model owner serves dictation first; meeting chunks, Annotate,
and `/streams` clients yield to it.

## Meetings, without a bot

Meetings is Hex's local recorder for calls. It sees a call start, offers to
record, and writes the result on your machine. It runs on macOS, Windows, and
Linux, off until you turn it on in the Meetings tab.

- Captures the microphone ("You") and system audio ("Them") at the same time.
  Remote speakers are not separated.
- Transcribes while the call runs, with live chapters, and stores a short title
  and summary when the Mac can write one. Details, decisions, and action items
  live in the transcript.
- Search is stemmed and fuzzy, so misheard names still match; quote a phrase to
  require it exactly.
- The transcript can be copied as Markdown, SRT, or VTT, or handed to an agent
  as a prompt that keeps reading as the call goes on.
- Meetings are kept 7 days by default; the choices are 24 hours, 7 days, 30
  days, or forever. Audio follows the meeting unless a separate audio retention
  is chosen. Expired meetings move to the Trash, and exported Markdown is never
  touched.
- Calendar matching links a recording to the event it belongs to.

Meetings is a feature you turn on; Hex never records a call silently and never
sends one anywhere.

## MCP: meetings for your agent

`hex mcp` is a local MCP server over stdio. It reads the meetings folder and
needs no running Hex, no login, no API key, and no network.

Tools:

| Tool | What it returns |
| --- | --- |
| `list_meetings` | Meetings newest first: id, title, start, duration, status, transcript kind, participants, whether notes exist. Filters: `since`, `until`, `query`, `limit` (default 20, max 200), `include_in_progress`. |
| `search_transcripts` | Ranked passages with meeting id, title, speaker, offset, absolute time, snippet, and match counts. Fuzzy and stemmed by default; `meeting_id` narrows to one meeting; `limit` defaults to 10, max 50. |
| `get_transcript` | Merged You/Them turns with mm:ss offsets and local clock times. Optional `start`/`end` (or `from`/`to`), `speaker` (`you`, `them`, `all`), `max_chars` (default 20,000), and `cursor` to continue. |
| `get_meeting_notes` | The stored title and a summary of at most two sentences. Never generates notes. |
| `get_chapters` | Topics with a name, one line, and start and end offsets, for meetings recorded with live chapters. Never generates chapters. |

Resource: `hex-meeting://<meeting_id>` returns that meeting's metadata, stored
notes, and transcript as Markdown.

Setup:

OpenCode, in `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "hex": {
        "type": "local",
        "command": ["hex", "mcp"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code:

```sh
claude mcp add hex -- hex mcp
```

Claude Desktop and Cursor share the `mcpServers` shape:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "hex": {
      "command": "hex",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Desktop reads
`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` on macOS and
`%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` on Windows. Cursor reads
`.cursor/mcp.json` in a project or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` for every project.

`hex mcp --meetings-dir <path>` reads a copy of a meetings folder elsewhere,
such as a mirror pulled from a laptop. A binary named `hex-meetings-mcp` always
serves meetings with the same flags.

## Annotate

Annotate captures a screen, a window, a region, or a connected iPhone, then
opens the capture in an OpenCode session. Captures are stored as
`.hexannotation` packages with the dictation-timeline audio, so a spoken
walkthrough and the screen line up. Annotate is on in every build; organizations
can turn it off with the managed key `DisableAnnotate`.

## Transforms

Transforms are JavaScript or TypeScript functions in
`~/.config/hex/hex.config.ts` that change dictated text before Hex pastes it.
Create the file with `hex commands init`; it writes types, `AGENTS.md`, and a
`tsconfig.json`.

```ts
import { defineHexConfig } from "@hex/commands"

export default defineHexConfig({
  transformations: {
    "trim-whitespace": {
      name: "Trim whitespace",
      description: "Remove leading and trailing whitespace",
      timeout: 1000,
      transform: (text, context) => text.trim(),
    },
  },
})
```

- The config reloads about a third of a second after a file changes. A config
  that fails to load keeps the previous one.
- `context` describes the foreground app, browser host and URL, window title,
  and whether the text came from dictation or the typed-text lab.
- A script gets `fetch`, `node:child_process` (`exec`, `execFile`), and
  `node:util`, but no filesystem, environment, `process`, or npm packages.
- `fetch` and `node:child_process` reach the network only after Hex approves
  the config's exact content hash. Managed Macs can restrict transforms to
  loopback or turn them off entirely.
- Transforms run in the order the person selects in Output, after word
  replacements and an optional AI rewrite.

## Command line

```sh
hex status --json                     # what Hex is doing, and this OS's capabilities
hex dictation start|stop|toggle
hex dictation stop --print             # print the transcript instead of pasting
hex transcribe meeting.m4a             # a file, whether or not Hex is running
hex settings list|get|set              # every persisted setting, dotted keys
hex settings set dictation_hotkey menu
hex history --since 7d --json
hex history --search 'problems board'
hex meetings list --since 7d --json
hex meetings show latest --md
hex meetings show latest --srt > call.srt
hex meetings chapters latest --json
hex meetings search 'release schedule'
hex mcp
```

- Control commands drive the running app through its owner-only local API and
  a bearer token; every command takes `--json` and returns a stable exit code.
- `hex history`, `hex meetings`, and `hex mcp` read files. They never launch
  Hex. Only `hex start` and `hex restart` open it.
- `hex transcribe` reads WAV, AIFF, CAF, FLAC, MP3, Ogg, WebM, and
  MP4/M4A/MOV, including a video's soundtrack.

## Privacy

- Audio is not persisted by default. Keep recordings is an explicit opt-in.
- Event logs never contain dictated text, full URLs, or window titles.
- History is the only dictation text store, kept 7 days by default and capped.
- Meetings and their audio expire to the Trash on your schedule; exported
  Markdown is never deleted by retention.
- Hugging Face searches are header-only, on demand, and read-only.
- No account, no cloud transcription, no in-app telemetry. Usage is measured by
  release downloads, not by the app.

## Managed Macs

Configuration-profile keys in the `anomaly.hex` domain can disable Meetings,
Annotate, OpenCode processing, transforms, Labs, and updates, or hold transforms
to loopback. They are macOS only; Windows reads only `DisableUpdates`, and
Linux reads none. A locked feature reads as off everywhere and refuses the CLI
and local API. Removing the profile restores the person's own settings.

## Labs

Labs are features Hex is trying out. Each is off until it is turned on in
Settings › Labs or with `hex labs on <id>`. They are listed, with one page
each, at https://anoma.ly/hex/labs. Stable builds never list Dev-only labs.

## Linux

Hex for Linux is a beta for x86_64 (AVX2) and ARM64 with glibc 2.36 or later.
It runs on X11 and on Wayland through one general path: `wtype` and
`wl-copy` on wlroots compositors (Hyprland, Sway) and niri, the
RemoteDesktop portal on GNOME and KDE Plasma, and the GlobalShortcuts portal or
your own keybindings running `hex dictation start|stop|toggle` for shortcuts.
On Hyprland and Omarchy, bind `anomaly.hex:dictation`. Transcription uses
Vulkan on the GPU or the CPU; the window needs a Vulkan driver. Meetings
records each output's PipeWire monitor. Page: https://anoma.ly/hex/linux

## Compared with other dictation apps

These pages compare Hex with each app's own public pages, read on
November 28, 2026, and say when the other app may fit better.

- Hex vs Wispr Flow: https://anoma.ly/hex/vs-wispr-flow. Wispr Flow
  transcribes in the cloud and needs an internet connection; Hex transcribes on
  the computer and works offline. Wispr Flow has a free plan with limited
  dictation and a paid Pro plan, runs on Mac, Windows, iPhone, and Android, and
  has a no-bot Notetaker and a remote MCP server. Hex is free and open source
  and also runs on Linux.
- Hex vs Superwhisper: https://anoma.ly/hex/vs-superwhisper. Both run local
  models. Superwhisper is closed source, free with local Whisper models, with
  Parakeet, cloud models, and AI modes in Pro; its Linux app is Wayland only,
  and its meetings, CLI, and MCP are on the Mac. Hex includes Parakeet for free,
  supports X11 and Wayland, and has meetings (Windows and Linux in beta), the
  CLI, and `hex mcp` on Mac, Windows, and Linux. Superwhisper runs on Intel
  Macs and macOS 14; Hex needs Apple silicon and macOS 15.

## Common questions

**Is Hex free?** Yes. MIT licensed, no account, no subscription, no word limit.

**Does Hex work offline?** Yes, after the one-time model download. Dictation and
meeting transcription make no network request.

**Which models?** Parakeet and Whisper GGUF models, Apple Speech on the Mac, and
custom models you add.

**Does a bot join my meetings?** No. Hex records the microphone and system audio
itself; nothing joins the call.

**Can my agent read my meetings?** Yes, with `hex mcp`, read-only over stdio.

**Where is my data?** On your machine. macOS keeps it under
`~/Library/Application Support/hex/`; Windows uses `%APPDATA%\hex` and
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\hex`; Linux uses `~/.local/share/hex`.

**What does Hex not do?** It does not join calls, transcribe meetings it did not
record, separate remote speakers, or send audio to a cloud service.
